issues.failure_explanation: For the stick-slip relation with r=2, the graph contains points (v,s)=(0,s) with |s| up to mu_star. The stated r=2 coercivity would then require 0 >= c(|s|^2-1) for all such s, which is impossible whenever mu_star>1. The same normalized '-1' obstruction applies to the shifted 2-coercive graph in Example ex:Fang when mu(0)=a>1.

failure_location.quote: For $\gamma_\star>0$ it is straightforward to see that $\gbd$ satisfies  Assumption~\ref{assump:gbd-mon} with $r = 2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the coercivity bounds in Assumptions assump:gbd-mon and assump:gbd-reg with an arbitrary additive constant (equivalently normalize the threshold), since the later estimates only absorb this constant.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed coverage of stick-slip and of the shifted Fang relation for arbitrary thresholds mu_star>=0 or a>b>=0 is unsupported; with the normalized coercivity bound only threshold radius at most one is covered.
issues.title: Coercivity offset excludes thresholds larger than one
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local constant/offset change; all proofs merely absorb the constant, so the method, conclusions, and advertised boundary-condition scope survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathcal{R}(\Omega) \coloneqq \operatorname{ker} \BD =  \{\bx \mapsto A\bx + \bb \text{ for some } A \in \setR^{d \times d} \text{ with } A = -A^\top \text{ and } \bb \in \setR^d \}.
we use the preceding inequality on each of the finitely many connected components and sum over the latter.

issues.failure_explanation: On a disconnected Omega, ker D contains independent rigid motions on different components, not only one global affine map x->Ax+b. For two disjoint disks, taking u to be a rotation about the center on one disk and u=0 on the other gives Du=0 and tr(u).n=0 on the whole boundary, while u is nonzero; the displayed estimate fails. Summing the connected-component inequality does not control these independent component rigid motions.

failure_location.quote: The same conclusion holds true if $\Omega\subset\R^{d}$ is open and bounded with Lipschitz boundary and has finitely many connected components.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the disconnected supplement, or restate it with the norm condition imposed on the full piecewise-rigid kernel of each connected component.
issues.overall_effect: Only the optional finitely-many-components supplement is unreliable; the connected-domain Korn inequality used later in the paper is unaffected.
issues.title: Disconnected-component supplement ignores independent rigid motions
issues.why_classification: The supplement is extra generality and is bypassed by the connected-domain assumption used in the convergence proof; the correction is local.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose that $\pi(x)\coloneqq Ax+b$ satisfies $\pi=0$ on $\Gamma$, whereby $\pi=0$ on $H_{1}\cup H_{2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption assump:dom requires pi.n=0 on Gamma, not pi=0 there. In dimension d=3, take two boundary patches in planes with normals e1 and e2 and the constant rigid translation pi=e3; then pi.n=0 on both patches but pi is nonzero. The proof tests the stronger condition pi=0 and therefore needs an additional hypothesis ruling out translations tangent to all supporting planes, e.g. that the relevant normals span R^d.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two-hyperplane condition by the requirement that the normals on Gamma span R^d (equivalently, no nonzero rigid translation is tangent to Gamma), and prove the estimate from pi.n=0 rather than pi=0.
issues.overall_effect: The stated simple two-normal sufficient criterion is false for d>=3; the full-boundary polyhedral Korn estimate used later remains true because the facet normals of a bounded polyhedron span R^d.
issues.title: Two non-collinear normals do not imply the rigid-deformation norm property
issues.why_classification: The correction strengthens a local geometric hypothesis; the Korn theorem and the polyhedral full-boundary application used in the convergence proof survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed local stability estimate cannot hold with an h-independent constant. For a linear function v, PiSZ v=v; on a face F of an element of size h the left side scales like |grad v| h^{(d-1)/2}, whereas the unweighted local H^2 norm over the patch is only O(|grad v| h^{d/2}) up to lower-order terms. The global boundary estimate used later is instead a direct consequence of the continuous trace theorem H^2(Omega)->L^2(partial Omega) plus the approximation-error estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove or correctly h-weight the local stability estimate, and prove the global estimate directly from the continuous H^2-to-L^2 boundary trace inequality and the error estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The local face stability statement is false; the global Scott--Zhang boundary stability actually used in the limit passage survives by the standard trace theorem.
issues.title: Unweighted local Scott--Zhang boundary stability is false
issues.why_classification: The repair deletes a false local side estimate or proves the used global estimate by a standard trace argument; no downstream convergence step is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: For piecewise constant pi^k and p=8/(d+4), Lemma lem:p-est controls delta_k^2 sum_j ||pi_j^k||_2^p = delta_k ||pi^k||_{L^p(I;L^2)}^p, not ||pi^k||_{L^p} or ||xi^k||_{L^p}. A scalar mean-zero pressure spike pi_1^k=delta_k^{-a} q with 1<a<2/p and pi_j^k=0 for j>=2 satisfies the controlled quantity delta_k^{2-ap}->0 but gives xi^k(t)=delta_k^{1-a}q for t>delta_k, which diverges. Thus the asserted uniform L^p bound for the time-integrated pressure does not follow.

failure_location.quote: By Lemma~\ref{lem:p-est} we have that \norm{\xi^k}_{L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2(\Omega))} \leq c,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a genuine uniform bound for the time-integrated pressure, for example by strengthening Lemma lem:p-est to control delta_k sum_j ||pi_j^k||_2^{8/(d+4)} or by recovering the pressure through a separate discrete pressure equation; the present delta_k^2 estimate is insufficient.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of xi in L^{8/(d+4)}(I;L^2(Omega)) and the stated weak pressure convergence are unsupported; consequently the pressure-recovery step used to derive the distributional limiting equation in Proposition prop:limit-eq is unreliable, while the velocity compactness estimates are not directly affected.

issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial pressure estimate or recovery argument is needed; the velocity/trace compactness and boundary-term identification remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
From the exponents we see that admissibility of 
a solution as test function 
is lost in dimension $d = 3$.

issues.failure_explanation: In d=3 the weak solution regularity gives only u in L^{8/3}(I;L^4) and the paper itself notes that a solution is not admissible as a test function. The cited truncation/mollification sentence supplies no commutator or extra regularity estimate; from the stated regularity for 3D Navier--Stokes one obtains the standard energy inequality, not the asserted equality. The equality is then used with the wrong inequality direction unavailable for the Minty limsup step in the r>2 antisymmetric identification.

failure_location.quote: one may employ a truncation and mollification in time to prove an energy identity for almost all times

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict the energy-identity-based r>2 identification to d=2 or add a regularity hypothesis (for instance u in L^4(I;L^4(Omega))) that makes the solution an admissible test function.
issues.overall_effect: The a.e.-time energy identity in dimension d=3 is unsupported, and the Minty identification for the antisymmetric method with r in (2,2^sharp) is not proved in d=3; the advertised d=3, r>2 convergence regime becomes unreliable.
issues.title: Energy identity is asserted in 3D without admissibility
issues.why_classification: The source offers no argument overcoming the loss of test-function admissibility in d=3; the only supported resolutions change an energy equality to an inequality or exclude the advertised d=3, r>2 regime.
